title: Collatz deep-machinery source manifest
deduplication_note: 58 chapter citation records become 56 main unique works after merging Bernstein–Lagarias and Bell–Ghioca–Tucker duplicates. scope: Consolidation of team-inspected primary literature and chapter-specific applicability analysis. A checked statement is not a complete proof audit, an independent formal build, or a proved Collatz bridge.

evidence_labels.full_text_statement_read: Full text: relevant theorem statements and hypotheses read; not a complete proof audit.
evidence_labels.primary_indexed_statement: Complete statement read in indexed primary-source text; direct full-file access was unavailable.
evidence_labels.author_exposition: Precise author exposition inspected; distinguish it from the original paper.
evidence_labels.later_primary_statement: Statement inspected in a later primary paper; original item checked bibliographically.
evidence_labels.primary_abstract_statement_read: Statement inspected in a primary publisher or official abstract; full proof not inspected.
evidence_labels.lead_researcher_statement_inspected: Statement or publisher abstract inspected by lead researcher; no full-proof audit claimed.
evidence_labels.primary_introduction_lead: Primary introduction/bibliography inspected; not an executable numerical theorem premise.
evidence_labels.bibliographic_framework_lead: Bibliography or general framework inspected; no specific technical theorem imported.
evidence_labels.primary_indexed_abstract_lead: Indexed primary abstract/metadata only; full text unavailable and no theorem imported.

metadata_policy: Publication year is preferred. Initial-preprint year is marked when no journal year was established. Version fields pin corrections and author versions. Null means not transcribed, not absent. Chapter aliases are retained verbatim; R01–R12 are crosswalk aliases for existing root-chapter tags.
original_deductions_are_not_source_theor: Polylogarithmic band-entry clock from effective logarithm separation.
OPEN-FLOOR exponent comparison using predecessor density.
